# UNITY201 lookup-in-hot-code

A component or object lookup (GetComponent, Find, Camera.main) in code Unity runs every frame.

## What it does

Fires in a Unity C# file (one that names `UnityEngine` or a `MonoBehaviour`) for `GetComponent`, `GetComponentInChildren`, `GetComponentInParent`, their plural forms, `TryGetComponent`, `FindObjectOfType` and its kin, `GameObject.Find*`, `transform.Find` and `Camera.main`, made in a per-frame callback (`Update`, `LateUpdate`, `FixedUpdate`, `OnGUI`, `OnAnimatorMove`, the `*Stay` collision and trigger messages) or in a method of the same class that such a callback calls, transitively. `Awake`, `Start` and `OnEnable` run once, so a lookup there is clean, and so is a helper reached only from them. A lazy cache (assigning a field from the lookup under an `if` that tests null, or with `??=`) is exempt. A coroutine helper is not followed, and a `Find` method the class defines itself is followed rather than reported. A plain .NET class that names no Unity type is not examined. The rule is Advisory.

## Why it matters

A lookup walks the component list or the whole scene on every call. Done every frame it costs time that grows with the scene and shows up as frame-time spikes.

## Remedy

Look the object up once in `Awake` or `Start`, keep it in a field, and use the field in the hot callback.

## Examples

### Fires case 1

```csharp expect=fire file=Assets/Scripts/Mover.cs
using UnityEngine;

public class Mover : MonoBehaviour
{
    void Update()
    {
        var body = GetComponent<Rigidbody>();
        body.AddForce(Vector3.up);
    }
}
```

### Fires case 2

```csharp expect=fire file=Assets/Scripts/Follow.cs
using UnityEngine;

public class Follow : MonoBehaviour
{
    void LateUpdate()
    {
        Track();
    }

    void Track()
    {
        transform.position = Camera.main.transform.position;
    }
}
```

### Clean case 3

```csharp expect=clean file=Assets/Scripts/Mover.cs
using UnityEngine;

public class Mover : MonoBehaviour
{
    Rigidbody body;

    void Awake()
    {
        body = GetComponent<Rigidbody>();
    }

    void Update()
    {
        body.AddForce(Vector3.up);
    }
}
```

### Clean case 4

```csharp expect=clean file=Assets/Scripts/Lazy.cs
using UnityEngine;

public class Lazy : MonoBehaviour
{
    Rigidbody body;

    void Update()
    {
        if (body == null)
        {
            body = GetComponent<Rigidbody>();
        }
        body.AddForce(Vector3.up);
    }
}
```
